title: Shelving unfinished work
summary: git stash: switch branches without committing half-done work.

say.never: Imagine you're halfway through something that isn't ready to save, and a teammate asks you to fix a small bug on another branch *right now*. Git won't let you switch branches if it would overwrite your unfinished work. A **stash** is a shelf: put your unfinished work on it, switch and fix the bug, come back, and take your work off the shelf.
say.bit: Stash shelves uncommitted changes so you can switch branches (git refuses to switch when your changes would be overwritten), then `stash pop` restores them.

say.never: Open the **terminal**: hold **Ctrl** and tap the backtick key (above **Tab**). Then type `cd 08-stash` and press **Enter**.

waitFor.hint: press Ctrl and the backtick key (above Tab).

say.never: Type `git checkout develop` and press **Enter**. Git refuses and says your local changes would be overwritten. That's exactly the problem a stash solves.
say.bit: Try `git checkout develop`. Git refuses: your changes would be overwritten.

board.code:
git checkout develop
# error: Your local changes would be overwritten

say.never: Type `git stash` and press **Enter**. Your changes go on the shelf. Now `git checkout develop` works. Change "Teh" to "The" in `Notes.md`, save, and commit it. Then `git checkout issue-21-new-motor` to go back, and finally `git stash pop` to take your work off the shelf.
say.bit: `git stash`, switch to develop, fix the typo and commit, switch back, `git stash pop`.

board.code:
git stash
git checkout develop
# fix Teh -> The in Notes.md, then:
git commit -am "Fix typo in pit notes"
git checkout issue-21-new-motor
git stash pop

say.never: Open the lesson chip and press **Verify** on **Stash**. It checks that develop has the fix, your unfinished line is back, and the shelf is empty.
